evidence: Levi–Bini p. 271: per tōtum annum scholasticum
terms.comment: Scholasticus, of the schools, is post-Augustan (Quint., Plin. Ep., Lewis & Short); the phrase is modern. At the start of the school year, ineunte annō scholasticō (see at the beginning of the year).

phrases.latin: Ineunte annō scholasticō novōs librōs ēmimus.
phrases.english: At the start of the school year we bought new books.

sources: Lewis & Short: annus · Lewis & Short: scholasticus
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 271.
